implementation_notes: Modern C++ makes the placeholder a value rather than a class: nullptr for pointer and smart-pointer slots, std::nullopt for optionals, a default-constructed Dummy{} where a reference to an object is required but never dereferenced, and a braced aggregate for struct parameters. [[maybe_unused]] is the callee-side complement - marking the parameter (or using an unnamed parameter) states that the implementation ignores it - while std::monostate is the standard-library unit type for the case where the type system demands a value (see the std-monostate variant). The classic Dummy class is still justified only where a reference or a template argument needs a complete type of the right shape, or where the placeholder should fail loudly instead of silently doing nothing.
code_sketch:
struct Unused {};                       // placeholder type for a required reference

Result run(const Config& cfg, Unused& /*unused*/);   // callee ignores the parameter

Unused dummy{};                         // the placeholder itself: no behaviour, no state
Session s{cfg, dummy, /*clock=*/nullptr, /*policy=*/std::nullopt};
s.execute();                            // this path reads none of them
pitfalls: A placeholder pointer or reference is an unchecked contract: a path that starts dereferencing the dummy is undefined behaviour, and a nullptr read can pass a debugger-free test run or be optimised away entirely.

Choosing std::monostate as the empty alternative forces every consumer of the variant to handle it; an unhandled alternative turns the placeholder into a runtime std::bad_variant_access instead of a compile error.
[[maybe_unused]] silences the compiler, not the reviewer: a parameter annotated for years hides an API that no longer needs the argument, so remove or default it once every path ignores it.

variants.name: std::monostate as the required-but-unused unit value
variants.implementation_notes: std::variant cannot be empty, so std::variant<std::monostate, A, B> uses monostate as its well-behaved empty alternative: the slot exists because the type requires a first alternative, and the value is never inspected on the paths that hold a real alternative. The same type serves as a unit value for a template parameter or a placeholder in generic code, where it is preferable to a hand-written empty struct because it is already complete, comparable and hashable. Reach for it when the placeholder is a *type* rather than an argument; use the core-language value forms (first variant) when a value of a concrete type can be passed directly.
pitfalls: monostate is not std::optional: it does not model 'absent' for the algorithm, it only fills a slot the variant requires, so callers must still decide how to interpret it.

A variant default-constructed into the monostate alternative can silently look like a valid state to code that only checks a subset of alternatives; validate the alternative index where the distinction matters.
